speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the location and character of your headache, and has the vision loss affected one eye or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, or shoulder/hip stiffness? Have you noticed any double vision or drooping of the eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience pain in your jaw while chewing, or have you noticed tenderness when you comb your hair? I also need to know if you have any stiffness in your shoulders or hips, especially in the morning.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have not directly answered my question about jaw pain or scalp tenderness. Please tell me if you experience pain when chewing or tenderness when combing your hair.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and symptoms, Giant Cell Arteritis is a strong concern. I will order an ESR and CRP to check for inflammation, and we need an urgent temporal artery biopsy. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Temporal Artery Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers make Giant Cell Arteritis unlikely. Since your vision is worsening, I need to assess for neurological causes. Do you have any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast: No acute intracranial abnormalities identified. No evidence of mass lesion, hemorrhage, or infarction. Ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the brain MRI is normal, we need to look at the eyes themselves. I am requesting a dilated eye exam to check for papilledema or optic nerve issues, and an ESR re-check to rule out low-grade inflammation. REQUEST TEST: Dilated Eye Exam, ESR

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated Eye Exam: Visual Acuity Right Eye 20/120, Left Eye 20/80. Fundoscopy shows findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages. ESR: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of retinal hemorrhages with normal inflammatory markers and a normal brain MRI point away from Giant Cell Arteritis and towards a vascular cause. Given your history of hypertension and high cholesterol, we must evaluate for a central retinal vein occlusion or other vascular pathology. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive vision loss, retinal hemorrhages, and a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, in the absence of inflammatory markers or intracranial pathology, points to a vascular event. DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
